content:
alex: Kicking off a short write-up of the GPTQ vs AWQ vs FP8/INT8 runs across Llama/Mistral/Qwen families. Sharing top-line eval deltas and a few deployment notes.

maya: Nice, can you include the exact eval set and the quant config you used?

alex: Sure — evals: MMLU (5-way), HellaSwag, BoolQ, ARC-easy, TruthfulQA (MC1). Baselines are model fp16 from our serving catalog. Quant configs: GPTQ 4-bit (per-channel, block=128, act-order=True), AWQ 4-bit (symmetric, group-size=128, act-order=False), INT8 symmetric and FP8 E4M3 using our fp8 toolchain.

jake: Top-line numbers? small table please (short).

alex: Quick bullets:
- Llama2-7b-chat (fp16 baseline): MMLU 58.2, HellaSwag 81.1, TruthfulQA 45.0
  - GPTQ-4: MMLU 57.5 (-0.7), HellaSwag 80.6 (-0.5), TruthfulQA 44.1 (-0.9)
  - AWQ-4: MMLU 56.9 (-1.3), HellaSwag 80.2 (-0.9), TruthfulQA 43.6 (-1.4)
  - INT8: MMLU 57.8 (-0.4), HellaSwag 80.9 (-0.2)
  - FP8: within noise (57.9, 81.0) but unstable on long context >2k tokens

- Mistral-7b-instruct (baseline): MMLU 61.0, HellaSwag 78.3, TruthfulQA 47.6
  - GPTQ-4: MMLU 59.4 (-1.6), HellaSwag 77.2 (-1.1), TruthfulQA 46.0 (-1.6)
  - AWQ-4: MMLU 58.0 (-3.0) — noticeably worse on reasoning tasks
  - INT8: MMLU 60.7 (-0.3) good tradeoff
  - FP8: Mistral tolerated FP8 slightly worse than INT8 on TruthfulQA (−1.9)

- Qwen-14b (chat tuned): MMLU 66.8, HellaSwag 84.5, TruthfulQA 52.2
  - GPTQ-4 (block256): MMLU 66.0 (-0.8), HellaSwag 84.0 (-0.5), TruthfulQA 51.5 (-0.7)
  - AWQ-4: MMLU 65.8 (-1.0) but faster encode times
  - INT8: MMLU 66.6 (-0.2)
  - FP8: parity with INT8 but occasional nan loss with act clipping off

priya: Those deltas look small for Qwen — any regressions detected during spot checks?

alex: Yes — two kinds of regressions found: 1) Answer hallucination increases on multi-hop prompts for GPTQ-4 on Mistral (we saw more confident wrong answers on ARC-style questions). 2) Tokenization edge-cases with Qwen when group-size small — generated trailing garbage for short prompts. Both are reproducible on specific seeds.

sarah: Any per-layer patterns?

alex: Yup — attention output and first FFN layers are the most sensitive. For GPTQ we saw larger weight outliers in the 2nd FFN -> recommend clipping or per-channel rescale. AWQ tends to hurt early attention heads in Mistral, so we used a hybrid config (AWQ for last 6 layers, GPTQ for first N) in one run with better overall stability.

jake: Deployment profiles? what to recommend for hosted vs dedicated?

alex: Notes:
- Hosted (latency-sensitive): prefer INT8 or FP8 when long-context (>2k) expected, because GPTQ-4 showed latency wins but higher regression risk on edge cases. Use continuous prefix caching + small batch (1–4) to hit SLOs.
- Dedicated (throughput): GPTQ-4 is cheapest in memory and token/sec on A100/4090 pools. We saw ~1.9x throughput vs fp16 for Llama2-7b on A100 with batch=8, seq=512.
- Private/on-prem: if customers want deterministic parity, recommend INT8 or hybrid GPTQ+FP16 fallback for risky routes.

priya: Any helpful commands/configs to reproduce?

alex: Paste of the quant step we used:
```
python tools/gptq/quantize.py \
  --model checkpoints/llama2-7b-chat \
  --out quant/llama2-gptq4 \
  --bits 4 --group-size 128 --act-order True \
  --calib-samples 2048 --verbose
```
and AWQ run:
```
python tools/awq/convert.py \
  --model checkpoints/mistral-7b \
  --out quant/mistral-awq4 \
  --group-size 128 --symmetric True --calib 4096
```

quant-bot: CI note — all reproduce runs are in 2024/12/quant-runs/ and artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-quant-bakeoffs/build-1851234567/ (models + eval logs).

sarah: Any suggestions for auto-deploy fallback policies?

alex: Yes — we should add a per-route quality gate: if the quantized model drops >1.5 MMLU points or >2% on truthfulness for a customer’s evalset, automatically route that customer's requests to fp16/dedicated until a manual review. Also add a sampling policy: 1% of live requests go to quantized variant for a week before rollout.

maya: Were any kernels or runtime flags important?

alex: We toggled act-order in the runtime and saw up to 0.6 MMLU delta on Mistral. Also enabling per-token KV cache prefetching reduced tail latency by ~15% on large chat histories. Use kernel flag: `--kv-prefetch=1` in runtime.

jake: Anything else unusual?

alex: One surprising find: FP8 on Qwen occasionally produced slightly better TruthfulQA scores than fp16 (small noise ~+0.2), but produced a rare NaN if we disabled activation clipping. So FP8 is promising but needs guardrails.

priya: Good notes. Can you add a short checklist for model onboarding?

alex: Onboarding checklist (short):
- Baseline fp16 evals on canonical suites
- Run GPTQ-4 & AWQ-4 & INT8 & FP8 (if available) with >2k calib samples
- Spot-check multi-hop + domain prompts used by customer
- Per-layer sensitivity analysis + hybrid config if needed
- Add 1% live shadowing + quality gate (>threshold rollback)
- Bake runtime flags (`--kv-prefetch`, act-order setting) into deployment profile

sarah: OK to push these notes to the docs repo as a short RFC?

alex: Yes, I'll open a tiny RFC in docs/quant-guides with links to the s3 artifacts and eval notebooks.

quant-bot: Upload complete: artifacts at s3://redwood-quant-bakeoffs/build-1851234567/manifest.json :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — super helpful. Can you include a minimal example of hybrid quant config?

alex: Example hybrid mapping (handy):
```
hybrid_config = [
  {"layers": "0-5", "method": "gptq", "bits": 4},
  {"layers": "6-20", "method": "awq", "bits": 4},
  {"layers": "21-xx", "method": "fp16"}
]
```
(we store these as simple YAML in `quant-configs/`).

jake: Perfect. That'll help infra rollout. Closing thread after RFC PR. :rocket:
